# 1. understanding the imported dataset

first, we need to understand the general structure of the data, including the number of observations, variables, and their data types

```{r}
# Loading the required packages
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)

# Loading the built-in mtcars dataset
data <- mtcars

# Checking the first six observations
head(data)

# Checking the last six observations
tail(data)

# Displaying variable names
names(data)

# Checking the structure of the dataset
str(data)

# Getting a general overview
glimpse(data)

# Checking the number of rows and columns
dim(data)
```

# 2. checking missing values and duplicate observations

before analysing relationships, we should check whether the dataset contains missing values or duplicated records

```{r}
# Checking missing values in each variable
colSums(is.na(data))

# Calculating the total number of missing values
sum(is.na(data))

# Checking duplicated observations
sum(duplicated(data))

# Removing duplicated observations if they exist
data <- distinct(data)

# Checking the dataset again
dim(data)
```

# 3. descriptive statistics

```{r}
# Summary statistics of the dataset
summary(data)
```

# 4. exploring individual variables

```{r}
# Histogram of fuel efficiency
ggplot(data, aes(x = mpg)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 10, fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Fuel Efficiency",
       x = "Miles per Gallon",
       y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()

# Boxplot of horsepower
ggplot(data, aes(y = hp)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "darkgreen") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Horsepower",
       y = "Horsepower") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 5. relationships between categorical and continuous variables

first, convert transmission into a categorical variable

```{r}
# Converting transmission into categories
data$transmission <- factor(data$am,
                            levels = c(0, 1),
                            labels = c("Automatic", "Manual"))
```

boxplot: fuel efficiency by transmission type

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = transmission, y = mpg,
                 fill = transmission)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Fuel Efficiency by Transmission Type",
       x = "Transmission",
       y = "Miles per Gallon") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## comparing horsepower by number of cylinders

```{r}
# Boxplot of horsepower by number of cylinders
ggplot(data, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = hp, fill = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Horsepower by Number of Cylinders",
    x = "Number of Cylinders",
    y = "Horsepower"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

comparing average fuel efficiency

```{r}
data %>%
  group_by(transmission) %>%
  summarise(Average_MPG = mean(mpg))
```

# 6. relationships between two continuous variables

scatter plot with regression line

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = hp, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Relationship Between Horsepower and Fuel Efficiency",
       x = "Horsepower",
       y = "Miles per Gallon") +
  theme_minimal()
```

correlation coefficient

```{r}
cor(data$hp, data$mpg)
cor.test(data$hp, data$mpg)
```

# 7. correlation between continuous variables

```{r}
# Selecting continuous variables
numeric_data <- data %>%
  select(mpg, disp, hp, drat, wt, qsec)

# Correlation matrix
cor(numeric_data)
```
